title: Other axis combinations: sharm (x,z / x,-z) and sdfcube (x,y / y,x)
purpose: Covers the remaining branches of the molecular-axis construction (`form_eulerangles`) used by `sharm` and `sdfcube` [@epsrmanual]: first axis x, second axis z, -z or y, and a single-atom-type centre.
fortran: `sharm_rev2.f`: `run_sharm` (keywords, `nsumt` rule), `sharm` (centres, axes, pair loop, averaged molecules)
system: The EPSR-test configuration `200DMSO400Water.ato`: 200 DMSO (atoms S, C, C, O, 6 H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1, H1; SPC/E parameters [@berendsen1987]), 3200 atoms at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å, a model of the DMSO-water mixtures of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. `sharm` expands the orientational pair correlation function of a central and a second molecule type in rotation matrices coupled by Clebsch-Gordan coefficients; the coefficients g(l1,l2,l;n1,n2;r) are averages over all molecule pairs [@soper1994,@graygubbins1984]. `axes.SHARM.dat`: water (axes `x 2 3`, `z 2`) and DMSO (axes `x 4`, `-z 2 3`), l1, l2, l = 0-2, n steps 1 (97 coefficients). `sdfcube` histograms the centres of the second molecules, rotated into the frame of each central molecule (Euler angles from the axis definitions), on a cubic grid and writes the spatial density function as a Gaussian `.cube` file together with the averaged molecules (`-first.xyz`, `-second.xyz`). `axes.SDFCUBE.dat`: water (axes `x 2 3`, `y 2`) and DMSO centred on S (axes `y 4`, `x 2 3`), 13×13×13 grid (`mpixel 6`, `rmax 7`), `averagemol y`.
inputs: Input files written by hand from the keyword tables (`setup_symbols_*`), one `keyword value` per line, ended by `q`; `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied from EPSR-test.
verification: One pass. Compared: `axes.SHARM.h01` (97 coefficients, `nsumt 1`), `axes.SDFCUBE.cube`, the four xyz files and both updated input files. Reference build: `sharm`/`sdf` were rebuilt with one comma inserted in the run-time title format (`'(1h(,'//il1fmt`), since gfortran 15.2 otherwise stops with "Missing comma between descriptors" before writing the coefficients; all other programs are the unmodified reference binaries.
